title: Schedule C and rental loss — Marcus Bell
instructions: Marcus Bell, single, runs a consulting business as a sole proprietor and owns one rental house in which he actively participates. Compute his 2025 amounts. His MAGI for the passive loss allowance is **$130,000**, and he has no other passive income.

exhibits.title: Consulting business
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Gross receipts | 180,000 |
| Cost of materials resold to clients | 60,000 |
| Office rent | 24,000 |
| Wages of an assistant | 30,000 |
| Meals with clients (business discussed) | 4,000 |
| Tickets to sporting events for clients | 3,000 |
| Penalty for late filing of a state business registration | 800 |

exhibits.title: Rental house
exhibits.content:
- Rent collected: 24,000
- Mortgage interest, taxes, repairs, insurance, and depreciation: 38,000
- Personal use: none

rows.label: Rental loss before limitations (enter as positive)
How is Marcus's self-employment tax deduction taken?
options: Half of SE tax as an adjustment for AGI
All of SE tax on Schedule C
rows.answer: Half of SE tax as an adjustment for AGI
rows.explanation: The employer-equivalent half is an above-the-line deduction.

rows.label: If Marcus sells the rental to an unrelated buyer next year, the suspended loss is
options: Deductible in full in the year of sale
rows.answer: Deductible in full in the year of sale
rows.explanation: A fully taxable disposition releases suspended losses.
